newsitem.title: CANADA: American Sensors hit by US$1 mln lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: American Sensors hit by US$1 mln lawsuit.

text.p: American Sensors Inc's Chicago-based distributor, Klesman and Associates Inc, said late on Monday it is suing the Toronto-based manufacturer of smoke and carbon monoxide alarms for more than US$1 million in unpaid commissions.
Klesman said it filed a lawsuit in February against American Sensors to recover overdue sales commissions earned by Klesman for its sales of American Sensors products.
In response to the lawsuit, American Sensors said last week it was "taking an aggressive position to take tighter control of its destiny" by parting company with Klesman.

In a termination letter to Klesman, American Sensors President and Chief Executive Michael Lupynec said his company considered the launching of the lawsuit by Klesman against American Sensors to be "gross misconduct and a unilateral breach of the contract," Klesman said.

On the heels of the lawsuit, the troubled American Sensors said late last week that its Canadian banker, Toronto-Dominion Bank, served a demand that American Sensors repay its outstanding credit facility. American Sensors said TD was owed about US$8 million.
The company said it had an offer from an asset-based lender that provided for an increase in its credit facility to US$22.5 million from US$20 million.
American Sensors' recent second-quarter balance sheet showed current assets of US$51 million and bank debt of US$13 million.
Klesman said it filed the lawsuit only after it made several demands and after meetings between management of both companies failed to resolve the matter of unpaid commissions.
The distributor also said the termination of its contract with American Sensors was based on an invalid argument.

"There is nothing in the sales representation contract between Klesman and Associates and ASI which prohibits the filing of a lawsuit by either party to resolve disputed issues. Nowhere in the letter dated March 12, 1997 was there any statement that Klesman and Associates failed in any way to perform according to the terms of the sales representation contract," Klesman said in a statement.

"Therefore, the reason given by ASI for the termination of the contract was without cause and this unilateral termination of the contract by ASI is in breach of the terms of the contract," Klesman added.

Klesman said it intended to pursue the payment of overdue commissions through the current lawsuit in addition to seeking damages from American Sensors the breach of the sales representation contract between the companies.
